title: [Spike] Graph projection — recursive SQL in Db2 or materialised in-process
summary: Decides whether PPR can run inline, how scope isolation is enforced on traversal, and what the memory footprint of the reasoning plane is.
description:
The entity graph over `memory_edges` has to be traversable. Two shapes with very different consequences. **Recursive SQL in Db2** keeps scope predicates in the query where the rest of the SDK puts them, adds no memory footprint, and requires no cache invalidation — but recursive CTE performance over a large edge table is unknown, and PPR's ~20 iterations become ~20 round trips unless the whole computation moves into SQL, which is awkward. **Materialised in-process** makes PPR trivially fast and lets us use a real graph library, but introduces a cache with invalidation, a per-scope memory footprint, and a second place scope isolation must be enforced correctly — which is precisely the kind of duplicated-invariant that produces cross-tenant leaks.

Evaluate with STOR-6's measured edge counts: recursive-CTE latency for 1/2/3-hop neighbourhoods at 10k and 500k rows; in-process build time and resident bytes per scope; cache invalidation cost under a realistic write rate; and how each behaves across multiple app replicas.

Timebox: one working session, ending in a DECISIONS.md entry. Depends on STOR-1, STOR-2, STOR-6. Blocks GRPH-3.
